clusters.name: Stepfather arrives, stepmother leaves over baby plans, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time Jonah began secondary school, his distance from his stepfather sharpened while his pull toward his father stayed warm. His stepmother and father separated over whether to have a baby, and Jonah made the chess squad but felt out of his depth—anxiety rising as the family shifted.

clusters.name: Grandfather dies, wrist injury ends playing, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Within months of each other, Jonah's grandfather died after years of illness, his father's parents reconciled after years of cutoff, and Jonah injured his wrist at conservatory and lost the ability to play. He leaned hard on his closest friend Rafe, then they clashed. His functioning fell, anxiety rose; he was high most days, absorbed in fixing radios, lost and low with no footing as his mother prepared to remarry.

clusters.name: Burnout from performing, grandmother's death and illness, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Over roughly two years, Jonah ran out of steam for performing and failed a disastrous audition for the national orchestra. Around the same time, his grandmother was found to have bowel cancer. He grew distant from family and friends, left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, then met Marisol and moved to Fenwick. They split within the year, and he sank into deep depression. He relied on friends rather than family, could not face his parents, then gradually began to recover through therapy and swimming. His grandmother died in early 2004; he visited her briefly before leaving town, hung over and anxious, and regretted the distance.
clusters.change: You moved through a major shift in your work and your sense of yourself as a performer, while your grandmother's serious illness and death ran alongside. The depression that followed the split with Marisol and your distance from your parents lasted into 2004, but you began to turn it around through therapy and friends, and by requesting help from your parents.

clusters.name: Both grandparents die, nursing school cutoff from mother, 2008
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Lorna died in early 2008, and your grandfather Clifford died around the same time. You took a break building with Silas before nursing school; your mother pressed to visit despite your repeated no, the visit went wrong, and you shut the door on her. When you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school that summer, you stopped speaking to your mother—the silence held for roughly a year. Around this time your aunt had a stroke.
clusters.change: The deaths of both your grandparents within months of each other came as you were preparing for nursing school. The conflict with your mother at Alder Creek and your decision to cut off contact when you moved away marked a sharper break than before.

clusters.name: Marriage to Wren, partner's family closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: You married Wren in spring 2017 and saw your mother a bit less afterward. Her brother Leo moved back nearby with his young children in 2019. Around late 2019, Wren became swamped with events and her family's demands piled up—a street party, a fundraising dinner, her mother's retirement at the lake. You overfunctioned to help settle her, tightening the plan. She fused closely with her father and brother; nothing happened to one that the others didn't hear. Your sleep worsened around her family occasions; you felt you didn't belong. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, and your aunt's memory loss worsened and she began lashing out.
clusters.change: Your marriage to Wren brought you into her family system, where her father, brother and she stay closely fused. As her family's events intensified in late 2019—her mother's retirement, her brother's return to the area—you felt the strain. Your sleep became your symptom; it worsens when you're around her family, and afterward you need long quiet drives home.
